title: Approximate Knowledge
synopsis: The Demon Cat leaves the dungeon to find out why his knowledge is only approximate, and drags Finn and Jake along.
plot:
The Demon Cat has grown tired of knowing many things almost. He knows that Finn is named Frank, Fred, or Finn. He knows the sky is blue, teal, or a color he has never seen. He decides to leave the dungeon for the first time in centuries to find the source of his knowledge and ask it to be more specific. He recruits Finn and Jake by threatening to eat their eyeballs, then admitting he is approximately sure he wouldn't.

Choose Goose sells them a riddle that points them to a well in the Grass Lands where 'the knower' lives. Along the way the Demon Cat's guesses cause chaos: he warns Jake about a bridge that is probably about to collapse, so Jake jumps off, and the bridge is fine. He predicts rain and it snows, briefly, on only the cat.

At the bottom of the well is a very old radio, still broadcasting fragments of a pre-war trivia show. The Demon Cat has been receiving it, faintly, through the dungeon rock for a thousand years. Finn offers to fix the antenna. The cat thinks about it, then declines. Knowing everything exactly sounds exhausting. He goes home, and tells Finn goodbye, Frank.
transcriptText:
Demon Cat: Greetings, Finn the Human Boy. Or Frank. Or Fred.
Finn: It's Finn. It's always been Finn.
Demon Cat: I know that. Approximately.
Jake: What do you want, cat?
Demon Cat: I want to know things for certain. Just once. I am leaving the dungeon to find out why I do not.
Finn: And you need us because...?
Demon Cat: Because I might eat your eyeballs. Or I might not. It is approximately fifty-fifty.
Jake: We'll come along.
Choose Goose: A riddle for the cat with the almost-hat! Where knowledge drips and echoes chat, look down, look down, where wet things sat!
Demon Cat: A well. Or a bathtub. Or a very sad lake.
Choose Goose: WELL DONE! Ha! Well!
[A rope bridge.]
Demon Cat: Jake. That bridge is about to collapse.
Jake: WHOA— [leaps off the bridge into the ravine]
[The bridge does not collapse.]
Demon Cat: ...Or it isn't.
Jake: [from the ravine] I HATE YOU.
Demon Cat: It will rain shortly.
[It snows, but only on the cat.]
Finn: Close.
Demon Cat: Close is my entire life.
[The bottom of the well. A rusted radio crackles.]
Radio: —for two hundred points, the capital of— kzzzt —is it a bird, a plane, or— kzzzt—
Finn: Dude. It's a trivia show. You've been picking up a trivia show through the rock for a thousand years.
Demon Cat: That explains the game show music in my dreams.
Finn: I can fix the antenna. You'd get everything. Every answer.
Demon Cat: [long pause] No.
Jake: No?
Demon Cat: If I knew everything, I would have nothing left to be wrong about. Goodbye, Frank.
Finn: It's FINN.
Demon Cat: I know.
